blueprint_topic: Management of Care — quality-improvement review using current STK-2 process-measure criteria
stem: A hospital stroke quality-improvement team notes a decline in STK-2, Discharged on Antithrombotic Therapy. Which action should the RN recommend first?

options.A: Review cases using the current STK-2 denominator exclusions and documented reasons for nonprescribing, then identify recurring process or documentation gaps.
options.B: Review ischemic-stroke discharges as potential care defects before applying the measure exclusions so nonprescribing cases are not missed during the audit.
options.C: Use the lower aggregate rate to begin staff education before reviewing individual records, then reassess the measure after the education is completed.
options.D: Revise the discharge pathway to default to antithrombotic prescribing and examine documented reasons for nonprescribing after the new pathway is in use.

rationale: A is correct. Joint Commission STK-2 version 2026B is a process measure for ischemic-stroke patients prescribed antithrombotic therapy at discharge. The measure defines the numerator, denominator, and denominator exclusions, including a documented reason for not prescribing antithrombotic therapy at discharge. Its data are reported as an aggregate rate. A quality-improvement review should therefore apply the current measure logic to case-level records before deciding what process or documentation problem is recurring. B is incorrect because classifying nonprescribing cases as potential defects before applying the measure exclusions can misclassify cases that are not in the measure population. C is incorrect because an aggregate decline identifies a performance signal but does not establish the cause or the appropriate intervention without case review. D is incorrect because changing the clinical pathway before analyzing the failed-measure cases risks treating the metric as a prescribing mandate and bypassing documented reasons for nonprescribing.
educational_objective: Use a declining stroke process-measure rate as a signal for structured case review: apply the current measure denominator and exclusions, examine documented reasons for nonprescribing, and identify recurring process or documentation gaps before selecting an intervention.

Version applies to discharges 07-01-2026 through 12-31-2026.
source_claim_supported: STK-2 is a current 2026B stroke process measure based on antithrombotic prescribing at discharge, with defined denominator exclusions including a documented reason for nonprescribing; the measure is reported as an aggregate rate and supports case-level quality review rather than automatic classification of every nonprescription as a care error.

targeted_near_duplicate_check: Repository-targeted search for 'STK-2 antithrombotic discharge quality improvement denominator exclusions reason not prescribing' returned no indexed matching files; no near-duplicate identified by the targeted check.
correction_summary: Retained the STK-2 quality-improvement construct but rebuilt the alternatives to remove the absolute-word distractor and blame-oriented/cartoon errors. The revised item tests realistic QI sequencing errors: auditing before exclusions, intervening from aggregate data without case review, and changing the pathway before understanding documented nonprescribing reasons.

option_audit.A: Correct; applies the current 2026B measure logic before causal interpretation or intervention selection.
option_audit.B: Plausible overinclusive-audit error; incorrect because the measure exclusions must be applied before treating a case as a performance failure.
option_audit.C: Plausible action-before-analysis error; incorrect because the aggregate rate does not identify the causal process gap or appropriate intervention.
option_audit.D: Plausible protocol-first error; incorrect because a QI team should understand measure failures and documented exclusions before changing the clinical pathway.

cueing_audit.absolute_words: No option relies on always/never/only/all/must-type absolutes.
cueing_audit.answer_length: All four options contain comparable QI-process detail; the key is not uniquely signaled by length.
cueing_audit.grammatical_lexical: All four alternatives are parallel first-step recommendations for the same QI scenario.
cueing_audit.second_answer_risk: No defensible second answer identified after Joint Commission 2026B source-based reread.
